title: Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Beneficiary Designation Terms
content:
# Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Beneficiary Designation Terms

1. A beneficiary designation is effective on the date it is received and must be signed by the insured.
2. A phone request cannot change a beneficiary.
3. When no valid designation exists at death, the benefit is paid in this order of precedence: spouse; children; parents; executor of the estate; next of kin.

These terms apply to every Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) policy, whatever the coverage tier.

## The terms broken down

| Question | Term |
|---|---|
| From when does a new designation count? | from the date it is received |
| Whose signature does it need? | the insured's |
| Can it be made by telephone? | no; a phone request cannot change a beneficiary |
| Who is paid if there is no valid designation at death? | the first class present in the order: spouse, then children, then parents, then executor of the estate, then next of kin |

## Order of precedence, illustrated (hypothetical families)

*Each row assumes no valid designation exists at the insured's death.*

| Survivors | First in the order of precedence |
|---|---|
| a spouse and two children | spouse |
| no spouse; two children; both parents | children |
| no spouse or children; one parent | parents |
| no spouse, children or parents; an executor of the estate appointed | executor of the estate |

## Points of judgement

- *A designation signed by the insured is received on 3 March. From which date does it take effect?* From 3 March, the date it is received.
- *The insured calls to name a new beneficiary. Does the call change the beneficiary?* No. A phone request cannot change a beneficiary; a designation must be signed by the insured.
- *A family member mails a designation the insured did not sign. Is it a designation under these terms?* No. A designation must be signed by the insured.
